title: BudgetThing mobile-first PWA on Expo, Convex Cloud, and Clerk
one_liner: Ship an installable, online-only mobile PWA with the existing BudgetThing feel and one shared user/data model, while preserving the Expo native path for a later iOS release.
base_branch: verified HEAD after preserving the dirty import work

meta.current_release_scope: PWA first; desktop redesign and native iOS release are later work
meta.backend: Existing Convex Cloud deployment; no self-hosting in this plan
meta.auth: Existing Clerk identity; authenticated PWA only
meta.planning_authorization: This plan may be published and documented; implementation, Convex production deployment, EAS build, submit, DNS, hosting and commits remain separately authorized

extras.label: Git caveat
extras.value: Current machine cannot execute git until the maintainer accepts the Xcode license; do not accept it automatically.

story: BudgetThing already has the product logic, a mobile Expo UI, Clerk sign-in, and Convex Cloud data. The next product surface is an installable phone-first PWA that feels like the existing app, is online-only at launch, and uses the same account and ledger as the future native app. The current checkout contains dirty agent-import work, so PWA implementation must begin from a recoverable, verified baseline without silently committing or losing that work.
how_we_got_here: The final direction is mobile PWA parity first, therefore Expo and React Native Web rather than a permanent Vite fork; online-only launch, therefore direct authenticated Convex reads/writes rather than browser SQLite; existing Convex Cloud and Clerk, therefore no self-hosted backend or identity migration; one product, therefore one canonical user/data model; desktop redesign and App Store delivery remain later phases.
done_means: A signed-in customer can install BudgetThing on an iPhone browser, use the complete agreed mobile PWA flow with the existing visual language, and see canonical data shared with the existing native-sync protocol without accounting divergence. The PWA has tested authentication, server error/offline behavior, installation/update behavior, real-device iPhone acceptance, and a reversible release handoff. Native code paths and existing local-first mobile sync remain intact.

decisions.choice: Keep the existing dark, portrait-first BudgetThing visual language, five-tab order, navigation intent, typography hierarchy, and full-screen editing flows on phone web.
decisions.why: The first web surface is the same product for normal customers, not a desktop redesign. Pixel/behavior parity is a target to validate against the existing app; no percentage-complete claim is assumed.

decisions.choice: Extend the existing Expo Router and React Native Web repository using narrowly scoped `.web.tsx` adapters and web helpers.
decisions.why: It reuses the mobile UI, shared logic, Convex types, and future native target. A permanent Vite fork would create duplicate product and parity maintenance.

decisions.choice: Use direct, authenticated Convex Cloud queries and authoritative mutations for the initial web release; do not enable guest mode or browser SQLite/offline write queues.
decisions.why: Online-only scope is simpler and avoids presenting unsynced financial state. Native retains its existing SQLite/outbox protocol.

decisions.choice: Keep the existing Convex Cloud deployment and Clerk identity provider.
decisions.why: It preserves current Clerk subject IDs and canonical server data. Self-hosting Convex or replacing Clerk is outside this release.

decisions.choice: Use existing entity fields, integer-cent values, stable IDs, tombstones, sync versions, source provenance, and change-log semantics; add compatible purpose-specific server APIs beside the current sync APIs.
decisions.why: Native and web must observe one ledger. Replacing or bypassing the legacy sync contract would risk data loss and accounting drift.

decisions.choice: Keep `trip_share`, `trip_cashflow`, and `trip_settlement` as virtual per-runtime projections. The PWA never persists derived rows to Convex.
decisions.why: Current native derived rows are local-only and deliberately excluded from outbound sync. Persisting a second web-derived copy would double-count and conflict with native reconciliation.

decisions.choice: Inventory active native clients and choose a launch boundary: a later native adapter may upload canonical per-user overrides, while PWA v1 never silently guesses or globally forces a user account choice.
decisions.why: Existing overrides are device-local and cannot be recovered from Convex. Native-App-Store availability is not a prerequisite for PWA launch, so unresolved older-client behavior must be documented and feature-gated where necessary rather than hidden behind a parity claim.

decisions.choice: Defer desktop-specific navigation, density, and layout redesign.
decisions.why: Mobile installability and iPhone usability are the release objective. Responsive desktop refinements should be a later, separately planned product phase.

decisions.choice: Preserve Expo-native modules and shared routes; do not run EAS build/submit in this PWA plan.
decisions.why: Native iOS remains a future target after the Apple developer account is available, and repository rules reserve EAS/App Store execution to the maintainer.

decisions.choice: Use a recoverable snapshot/worktree procedure before implementation; do not auto-commit, discard, reset, or merge the existing import work.
decisions.why: The current branch has unreviewed dirty work. A clean feature worktree needs a known base without losing its tracked or allowlisted untracked source/assets.

research.summary: The current Expo project already declares React Native Web, React DOM, Expo Router static web output, a web HTML entry, Clerk, Convex, and the full mobile screen tree. The known incompatible pager component must be replaced on web, and direct native storage/date/modal dependencies need adapters. The existing Convex code stores authenticated data by Clerk subject and already owns the authoritative schema, shared-trip ACLs, API imports, and change log.
research.recommended: Keep one Expo repository and Convex/Clerk backend. Make web-specific shells for platform blockers, add direct server query/mutation APIs that preserve the existing contracts, and release only after iPhone Safari installed-PWA acceptance plus native-sync compatibility evidence.
risks: The current repository plan mixes historic/stale paths and status with current root files; inspect actual code before each implementation phase.
The current dirty import/API work must be preserved and explicitly selected, not inherited accidentally into PWA work.
The local machine's git commands are blocked by an unaccepted Xcode license, so baseline verification is a prerequisite owned by the maintainer; do not accept the license automatically.
Current device-local derived-account overrides cannot be recovered by the PWA. Exact override parity needs a later compatible native adapter or a deliberate per-user web selection/migration boundary.
Existing PWA config is incomplete: manifest/install icons, service-worker/cache policy, browser auth storage, and installed-app update handling need explicit implementation and real-device testing.
Financial correctness requires canonical server mutations to keep trip ledger/cashflow, transfers, tombstones, imports, and native sync behavior compatible.
Production hosting/domain and release account choices are not configured by this plan and must be supplied/approved at release time.

phases.title: Preserve the dirty checkout and establish the PWA baseline
phases.goal: Create a recoverable, content-verified PWA worktree without losing, committing, or contaminating the existing import work.
steps: Ask the maintainer to complete the Xcode license action outside this plan if git is still unavailable; do not accept it on their behalf.

Read `git status --short`, `git diff --binary`, `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git worktree list` after git becomes usable; record only paths, base commit, and hashes in a local execution log, never credentials.

Create a safe temporary snapshot root with `snapshot_root="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/budgetthing-pwa-snapshot.XXXXXX")"`; confirm it is outside this repository. Write the tracked binary patch and NUL-delimited pre-snapshot status there. Create a human-reviewed explicit allowlist manifest for untracked source/docs/assets that belong to the current import work. Exclude `.env*`, credentials, tokens, certificates, `node_modules`, build output, Pods, and database files.

Hash the patch and each allowlisted file, copy the allowlisted files to a local snapshot outside the repository, then compare source hashes and working-tree path manifest to prove the original checkout is unchanged.

Create `feature/mobile-pwa` from the verified base commit in a separate worktree. Do not apply the import patch there by default; only apply/copy explicitly chosen import files after their dependency status is reviewed.
Treat a reviewed commit as an alternative only if the user explicitly authorizes a commit. Never use reset, checkout, clean, stash, or automatic commit to create the baseline.
In the new worktree, install dependencies without writing lockfiles, inspect current route/build configuration, and record the exact PWA scope baseline.

Add the approved newest-first unchecked PWA checklist to `plan.md` only after this Planthing plan has been approved/published. Prepend surgically, then byte-compare the original `plan.md` suffix to prove no pre-existing text changed.

verification.plain: The original dirty checkout is unchanged and recoverable; the PWA worktree starts at an identified base with no accidental credentials, build output, or import changes.
verification.expect: Recorded hashes/manifests match before and after snapshot; the original checkout remains dirty exactly as it was; the new worktree has the verified base only; old `plan.md` content is byte-for-byte preserved after the new prepend.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Do not create or alter a worktree until the original dirty paths can be snapshotted and compared safely. Escalate the missing git/license prerequisite to the maintainer.

exit_criteria: A maintainer-verifiable snapshot and allowlist manifest exist outside the repository.
No secret, environment, dependency, build, Pod, or database file is copied into the snapshot/worktree.
The PWA worktree base commit and original checkout status are recorded.
The published plan is linked from a new unchecked checklist at the top of `plan.md`, with original suffix integrity proven.

phases.title: Prove the universal web runtime and auth shell
phases.goal: Make the existing Expo app run as an authenticated mobile web shell without changing native behavior.
steps: Produce a resolved import-graph audit from `app/_layout.web.tsx`: the web provider/data boundary uses web adapters such as `lib/hooks/useData.web.ts`, `useTrips.web.ts`, `useSharedTrips.web.ts`, `useUserSettings.web.ts`, `transactionFilterStorage.web.ts`, `app/import-inbox.web.tsx`, and `app/settings/api-import.web.tsx`. Prove it excludes SQLite, `lib/db`, sync engine, SecureStore, pager, native date picker, and native emoji modules.
Create platform-specific provider/auth/token-storage adapters so browser tokens/settings never call SecureStore directly; keep native imports and behavior unchanged.

Preferred default: first prove the existing Clerk Expo provider on web. Add a Clerk web-specific package only if the vertical slice demonstrates a concrete incompatibility, then isolate it behind the web shell without changing user identity semantics.
Add a web app shell that requires Clerk sign-in, supplies Convex auth, handles initial auth loading, and sends unauthenticated users through the approved login/onboarding route.
Define online-only runtime behavior: no guest mode, no guest seed, no browser SQLite bootstrap, no local outbox, and explicit signed-out/network/server-error views.
Keep all public runtime configuration limited to approved `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values; do not put deploy keys, admin keys, or Clerk server credentials in browser code.
Run the web bundle and test Clerk token refresh plus Convex authenticated request/rejection behavior using the development deployment only.

Before full feature work, run the no-write vertical slice on an actual iPhone Safari browser and record viewport, sign-in, realtime read, sign-out, user-switch privacy, and unsupported-dependency results.

Establish browser automation before feature work: add `playwright.config.ts`, `e2e/*`, and `test:web` scripts with Chromium and WebKit mobile/desktop projects, dedicated authenticated Clerk test users, per-run disposable Convex fixture IDs and cleanup, no production data, and screenshot/trace/video artifacts.

verification.plain: A signed-in browser receives authenticated Convex data; a signed-out browser cannot enter the ledger; native provider behavior remains buildable.
verification.expect: Web opens without native-module runtime errors; Clerk sign-in/session refresh reaches Convex; sign-out removes private data; the hosting headers/origins, browser matrix, and final release hostname input are recorded; typecheck and existing tests pass. Playwright setup creates isolated fixtures and screenshots for Chromium/WebKit; real iPhone remains a separate acceptance gate.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Resolve provider, token-storage, route-gate, or native-regression failures before implementing feature screens.

exit_criteria: Web authentication is browser-safe and authenticated-only.
No guest/offline persistence is accidentally active on web.
Native-specific credentials remain out of the web bundle.
Existing native tests/typecheck still pass.

phases.title: Add compatible direct Convex read and write APIs
phases.goal: Let the online PWA read and mutate the canonical ledger directly while preserving local-first native sync compatibility.
steps: Map every web-needed view and write to its existing canonical Convex table(s), identity scope, change-log behavior, soft-delete behavior, and native sync counterpart.

Before enabling PWA writes, prove native-created data can be read by one proposed web command and web-created/update/tombstoned data pulls into native with matching IDs, optional-field clearing, versions, order, totals, filters, and trip views. Block on this compatibility gate.

Add `convex/pwaAuth.ts` (`requireUser`, `requireOwnedLive`, `assertExpectedVersion`, server time/ID helpers), `convex/pwaValidation.ts` (integer cents, owner references, card/split/system-type rules), and a small write helper. Keep pure account/split/balance/summary/filter rules in shared `lib/logic`; do not duplicate accounting in UI.

Create purpose-specific reads: `convex/pwaPersonal.ts` (`listDashboard`, `listTransactions(filters,cursor)`, `listAccounts`, `listCategories`, `getSettings`), `convex/pwaTrips.ts` local list/detail read models, `convex/pwaSharedTrips.ts` member-scoped reads, and `convex/pwaImports.ts` pending imports. Each filters tombstones at its canonical boundary.

Create authoritative commands: `pwaPersonal` account/category/settings create/update/archive/reorder; `pwaLedger` transaction create/update/soft-delete/bulk-category, one-row transfer, and adjustment; `pwaTrips` trip/participant/expense/settlement create/update/archive/reorder/delete; `pwaSharedTrips` member/invite/expense/settlement commands; `pwaImports` confirm/ignore. Each accepts domain inputs plus optional expected revision, returns canonical row/revision or PWA structured conflict, blocks raw client `userId`/timestamps/syncVersion/derived types, and records personal changes with `recordUserChange` and shared changes with `recordTripChange`.

Keep web-derived trip rows virtual. Add a defensive query guard that excludes any malformed/legacy persisted `trip_*` row before merging the virtual projection, and add a contract test that derived local upserts/tombstones never enter native outbound sync payloads.

Preserve the existing `sync:push`, `sync:pull`, shared-trip sync, HTTP import API, stable IDs, `updatedAtMs`, `syncVersion`, tombstones, and provenance fields. Do not rename/remove existing endpoints or fields.

Add web-only `derivedAccountOverrides`, indexed by `(userId, sourceKind, sourceId, direction)` and containing owned `accountId`, `updatedAtMs`, `deletedAtMs`, and revision. Its owner-scoped get/set drives only PWA virtual projections. Do not emit this unknown entity through legacy change logs/sync until a versioned native adapter proves it safe; device-local native choices remain untouched and cannot be auto-imported.

Apply full authorization checks to every query/mutation and shared-trip membership action. Keep API keys hashed, one-time raw-key reveal rules, rate limiting, idempotency, and audit logging unchanged. Add an isolated Convex fixture/harness task and `test:convex` script before claiming integration coverage; it uses disposable dev fixtures and never production data.
Deploy only to the documented Convex development deployment after local tests and review. Production deployment is a later maintainer-authorized release action.

verification.plain: Web-originated canonical writes are authorized, idempotent where required, and visible to the native sync protocol without changing money/trip rules; no derived projection is persisted or outbound-synced.
verification.expect: All unit/rule tests pass; dev schema/functions deploy additively; authenticated and unauthorized smoke checks produce expected results; native/web round-trip fixtures match; current sync endpoints remain available; derived outbound exclusion contract passes.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Revert only the unverified phase changes in the PWA worktree and fix compatibility/authorization failures before any UI consumes the API. Do not deploy production.

exit_criteria: Every PWA write has a documented purpose-specific canonical server mutation and authorization rule.
Existing native sync receives PWA changes through compatible change-log records.
No web-derived transaction is persisted, and malformed persisted derived rows are excluded defensively.
No existing backend endpoint, table field, or import behavior is removed or weakened.
Rules tests cover all affected money/trip paths.

phases.title: Adapt navigation and shared chrome for phone web
phases.goal: Replace web-incompatible native paging with a mobile browser shell that retains BudgetThing’s existing navigation intent and visual language.
steps: Use the existing tab order exactly: Calculator, Transactions, Accounts, Trips, Settings; preserve selection behavior and the floating tab-switcher design intent.
Implement web replacements for root, onboarding, local-trip-detail, and shared-trip-detail pagers without importing `react-native-pager-view` on web.
Use browser history/deep-link behavior deliberately so close/back actions and nested account/category/settings paths work on mobile Safari and installed mode.
Create platform-specific modal/sheet, popup, blur, haptic no-op/progressive-enhancement, keyboard, safe-area, and date-input primitives where current native assumptions do not hold.

Preferred defaults: retain existing emoji picker only if the target-browser spike proves it works, otherwise use a bounded browser-native emoji input fallback; retain the existing font hierarchy with a documented web fallback stack unless licensed font assets are already present; add no new package without target-browser evidence.
Warn before browser navigation/reload when a server-backed form has unsaved edits; do not cache private form drafts as financial authority.
Preserve black background, orange accent, typography hierarchy, locked geometry/copy, touch target sizes, and portrait-first widths. Do not begin a desktop layout redesign.
Establish a screenshot/reference checklist against the existing iOS screens for every shared shell state.

verification.plain: The PWA has the same mobile navigation order and recognizable visual language without web pager crashes or broken browser back behavior.
verification.expect: Phone-width Safari/Chrome navigation reaches each tab and nested flow; no PagerView is rendered on web; screenshots meet the approved screen-by-screen reference checklist.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Correct web shell/navigation behavior before porting feature interactions, because every later screen depends on it.

exit_criteria: No web bundle path imports or renders an unsupported pager.
All five primary tabs, onboarding, nested paths, modals, and browser back behavior work on phone web.
The implementation remains mobile-first and does not claim unmeasured pixel parity.

phases.title: Connect calculator, transactions, accounts, categories, and settings to direct Convex data
phases.goal: Deliver the personal-ledger PWA flows with canonical online reads/writes and existing financial presentation rules.
steps: Build web data hooks over the direct Convex queries/mutations and keep shared pure formatters/calculators in `lib/logic`.

Port calculator expense/income creation, transactions grouping/detail/edit/delete, accounts/current balance, transfer, adjustment, category management, currency, filters, settings, profile and import-inbox entry points.
Ensure transfer stays one canonical transaction with from/to account IDs; adjustment stays a canonical adjustment; values stay integer cents end-to-end.

Apply Transactions visibility rules: always hide `trip_cashflow`, render trip share as `share · total` with muted total, exclude trip settlement from monthly spent totals, and prevent derived rows from bulk edit/delete.
Implement explicit online failure, retry, expired session, no-data, and mutation-pending states. Never present a saved state until the server mutation resolves.
Verify direct PWA changes appear after native pull and native changes appear in a live PWA session without duplicate records.

verification.plain: Core PWA ledger actions write one correct canonical record and render correct totals/visibility across a signed-in browser and native-sync client.
verification.expect: Expense, income, transfer, adjustment, edit/delete, filters, account balance, currency, and import entry routes pass the scripted browser matrix; rule tests pass; cross-client records converge without duplication.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Diagnose canonical mutation payload, change-log, totals, or visibility-rule failures before trips or PWA packaging.

exit_criteria: Core ledger screens do not depend on browser SQLite/local sync.
Money uses integer cents and canonical transaction types.
Required transaction display rules are covered by tests and browser scenarios.
Online error/retry states are usable and truthful.

phases.title: Deliver local and shared trip parity on web
phases.goal: Make trip creation, expense splits, balances, settlements, invitations, and derived accounting correct in the mobile PWA.
steps: Connect local trip list/detail/add/edit/participant, add-expense, split-editor, balances, and settlement flows to canonical server APIs without changing participant identity constraints.
Connect shared-trip list/detail/member/invite/join/add-expense/edit/settlement flows to existing membership-guarded server APIs and direct read models.
Use existing split calculator and derived accounting modules; cover equal, equal-selected, percentage, shares, and exact splits including remainder/banker-rounding behavior.

Enforce one current user for each local group trip. Inventory supported active native clients and establish the release boundary for device-local derived-account overrides: web may use an explicit per-user selection/canonical override only after design approval; it must never silently guess, overwrite, or globally force an account choice.
Keep share ledger rows accountless; charge real accounts only when the current user pays or settlement moves funds; derive those rows virtually in each runtime and never persist them to Convex.

If old native clients cannot consume a canonical override, document the limitation and feature-gate the affected group-trip web write flow or explicitly accept runtime-specific account projection. Do not require an unavailable App Store native update before PWA launch.
Validate deletion/reconciliation/idempotency and web/native canonical-data convergence for both local and shared trips.

verification.plain: Each trip split and settlement produces the correct canonical ledger and virtual cashflow result, is safe to reconcile repeatedly, and has an explicit tested boundary for any old-client device-local account override.
verification.expect: All five split types, payer/non-payer behavior, settlement movement, deleted canonical rows, invitations/membership ACLs, virtual-row non-persistence, and repeated reconciliation pass scripted tests and two-client scenarios; old-client override limits are documented rather than claimed as exact parity.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Treat any ledger/cashflow divergence, duplicate derived row, wrong account impact, or ACL leak as release-blocking; fix before PWA packaging.

exit_criteria: All `rules.md` trip contracts have automated coverage and browser evidence.
Local and shared trip behavior uses the same accounting model where required.
No derived transaction is persisted, bulk-editable, or bulk-deletable from the PWA.
The native-override compatibility boundary is tested and documented before group-trip web writes launch.

phases.title: Finish import inbox and cross-client compatibility
phases.goal: Ensure the API-import workflow and current native sync protocol remain safe after direct-web APIs are introduced.
steps: Review the dirty import feature as its own dependency and either bring an explicitly reviewed subset into the PWA worktree or leave it out with clear feature gating; never silently copy it.
If included, render pending inbox items, edit/confirm/ignore actions, duplicate flags, badges, and API-key management with browser-safe modal/clipboard behavior.

Keep structured-only imports separate from transactions until user confirmation. Server `confirmImport` atomically owns pending-to-confirmed finalization, uses the exact existing native deterministic transaction-ID algorithm, validates immutable provenance, creates/loads one canonical transaction, patches the inbox item, and records both changes. The v1 product remains review-first; unattended/direct posting is an explicit later non-goal.

Harden legacy `sync:push` import-linked handling as an authoritative state machine, not generic row LWW: a confirmed inbox accepts only its exact deterministic provenance transaction and ignores competing candidate fields; ignored-versus-confirm is conflict; pending native confirm requires matching provenance; amount/date/type/account/category are immutable after confirmation except through dedicated audited edit/reversal.

Run compatibility matrices for PWA direct mutation → mobile pull; mobile local mutation → PWA live query; import API → PWA inbox; web-first/native-first confirmation retries and contradictory payloads; confirmation/ignore races; deletion/account switch → authorization isolation. Prove old native conflict rejection is non-poisoning and its outbox does not retry forever.
Add high-impact dedupe grouping/canonical selection tests and rapid-save/reconcile/sync failure tests that remain outstanding in `plan.md` where they touch this release.
Document whether production agent API docs are release-ready only after the production backend deployment is explicitly authorized and verified.
As soon as the import inbox vertical path exists, execute API candidate to PWA review to confirm/refresh on an actual iPhone browser before the broader feature pass.

Exclude API-import provenance transaction/inbox pairs from generic LWW and process them as one authoritative import state-machine pass. Released native `sync:push` must retain its `{status:"ok"}` response, after which existing native broad `markAsSynced` runs before normal full `sync:pull`; do not invent a per-record legacy acknowledgement or toast.

For a same-user server-ignored inbox plus an incoming exact deterministic `api_import` provenance transaction, atomically insert or patch a canonical deleted resolution transaction at that id using server inbox immutable amount/date/type/account/category and provenance fields, set a server revision/tombstone, record user changes for BOTH ignored inbox and resolution transaction, and audit `import_sync_server_winner_ignored`. The next normal full pull is authoritative and must overwrite the native SQLite transaction with `deletedAtMs` and `needsSync=0`, removing it from transaction lists, account totals, and month totals.

For a server-confirmed item, only exact immutable provenance/financial fields are idempotent; conflict is a server-winner no-op with canonical winner change-log records. Missing, malformed, unpaired, or unattributable provenance never passes through generic LWW or creates an active record. A push-only old native session may remain temporarily stale until its next full pull. Data that cannot be safely attributed cannot be auto-repaired, so PWA import launch is feature-gated until a repair/migration boundary exists.

Exercise Hermes and actual Shortcut voice/keyword flows end to end: strict JSON request, Shortcut/Hermes voice or keyword capture -> persistent per-event UUID -> import POST -> status check -> open PWA inbox. Reuse the UUID for retry so one event creates one candidate/transaction; two independent identical purchases carry distinct UUIDs and both post. Run both paths on a real iPhone.

verification.plain: Imports are authenticated, review-first, idempotent, auditable, and atomically finalized; web and native clients converge on one matching terminal inbox row and provenance transaction without duplicate, contradictory, cross-user, or endlessly retried records.
verification.expect: Validation/idempotency/dedupe tests pass; unauthorized and malformed API requests are rejected; a valid candidate remains pending until confirmation; web-first/native-first and race fixtures create exactly one immutable source-tagged transaction and one matching terminal inbox row visible to both clients; rejected old-native transitions do not retry forever. The integration fixture performs released SQLite confirm -> `sync:push` status ok -> broad mark-as-synced -> full pull and asserts the correction tombstone, `needsSync=0`, ignored inbox, and exclusion from native transaction list/account/month totals.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Do not expose or document production API use until the failing authorization, duplicate, audit, or confirmation path is corrected.

exit_criteria: Import work is either explicitly included and tested or explicitly excluded/feature-gated.
No API key, raw payload, or secret is exposed in PWA code, logs, tests, or plan artifacts.
The included import vertical path passes on an actual iPhone browser before full PWA release QA.
Cross-client high-impact write paths have passing duplicate/failure tests.

phases.title: Make the web app installable and operationally honest
phases.goal: Provide install, update, auth, cache, and connection behavior appropriate for an online-only finance PWA.
steps: Add a web manifest, appropriate phone install icons, theme/background metadata, and manifest link through the Expo web HTML entry.

Preferred default: minimal static-shell service-worker cache for public app assets only; never cache Clerk/session material, Convex responses, HTTP import API responses, or financial mutations. Show a clear connection-required/retry state for all data requests.

Implement installed-PWA update signaling and safe reload behavior so a new release does not falsely report stale financial data as current, and warn before refresh/navigation when a server-backed form is dirty.
Verify Clerk authentication redirects/cookies/storage in browser and installed contexts; configure redirect/allowed origins only after the release hostname is an explicit approved input.
Add connection-loss, Convex maintenance/error, token expiry, storage-unavailable, and unsupported-browser messages with retry/sign-out behavior.
Test iPhone Safari browser, installed home-screen PWA, and Android Chrome. Test desktop only for graceful non-goal behavior, not redesign parity.

On iPhone Safari over HTTPS, execute Share -> Add to Home Screen -> Open as Web App -> Add -> launch -> login/navigation -> logout; then verify refresh, browser Back, and second-account switch expose no previous private financial UI/data. Permit Clerk SDK session storage only, and inspect service-worker caches to confirm no app-created finance/auth payload cache.

verification.plain: A customer can install the PWA on a real phone, sign in safely, receive current server data only while online, and understand update/offline/auth failures.
verification.expect: Manifest passes browser inspection, install prompt/home-screen installation succeeds, installed and browser modes authenticate, update behavior is visible, and loss of network never exposes an editable stale local ledger.
verification.on_fail: Stop. Fix install, cache privacy, update, or phone-auth behavior before release review; do not compensate by claiming offline support.

exit_criteria: The PWA is installable on the agreed real devices.
Cache policy is documented and consistent with online-only financial data.
Auth and error states work in installed and browser contexts.
No hostname/provider/account is configured without explicit release authorization.

phases.title: Audit the mobile PWA and prepare a maintainer-controlled release
phases.goal: Produce evidence that the PWA is ready for a controlled hosted release without deploying, committing, or building native artifacts automatically.
steps: Run full unit, type, lint/doctor if configured, web export, and dev-deployment smoke checks after all PWA changes; resolve failures before review.

Execute a phone-first acceptance matrix on actual iPhone Safari and installed PWA: sign-in/out, onboarding, all five tabs, calculator, accounts, transaction detail, filters, local/shared trips, all split types, settlements, import inbox if included, API-key management, refresh/update, token expiry, offline/error, and browser back/deep links.
Perform an exact screen-by-screen visual review against the existing mobile app for agreed flows. Record measured differences/accepted deviations; do not state a fabricated parity percentage.
Execute cross-client data matrix with the existing native app/local sync and PWA on the documented development deployment, including user switch and duplicate/concurrency scenarios.

Prepare a release runbook with explicit maintainer inputs: approved web host/domain, production environment values, Clerk redirect/origin changes, production Convex backup, production backend deploy command, web artifact upload/hosting command, monitoring, rollback, and post-release smoke checks.

Request explicit maintainer approval before any commit/push, Convex production deploy, DNS/hosting write, EAS build/submit, or App Store action. Those actions are outside planning authorization and must stay separately controlled.
After implementation is actually complete, update the PWA checklist in `plan.md` phase-by-phase; preserve all older plans and verify the final package/worktree state.

Use additive, backward-compatible schema migrations only: before production promotion export/backup and rehearse restore into an isolated target. Roll back web behavior by serving the prior artifact and/or disabling the web-write feature flag. Never destructively restore or roll back production financial data to undo an app release; retain changelog/tombstones and repair with audited compensating, data-forward operations.

verification.plain: The release candidate passes automated, cross-client, and actual-iPhone PWA acceptance; deployment is a reviewed maintainer decision with a rollback path.
verification.expect: All checks pass; acceptance evidence identifies actual devices/browsers and outcomes; release inputs and rollback are documented; no production, hosting, git, or EAS action occurs without a distinct maintainer authorization. The pre-production export and isolated-target restore rehearsal, prior-artifact/feature-flag rollback drill, and data-forward correction path are documented and evidenced.
verification.on_fail: Stop release preparation at the failing check, fix in the isolated PWA worktree, and repeat the relevant matrix. Do not deploy around a failed accounting, auth, cache, or real-device test.

exit_criteria: Automated tests, export, dev smoke, cross-client checks, and actual iPhone acceptance pass.
Visual differences are recorded rather than hidden behind a parity claim.
Release host/domain and production steps are approved inputs, not guessed configuration.
Maintainer has a concrete release and rollback runbook.

acceptance: The release is a customer-facing, installable, authenticated mobile PWA; it is not an offline/guest app or desktop redesign.
The existing tab order is Calculator, Transactions, Accounts, Trips, Settings and the established black/orange mobile visual language is retained for approved phone flows.
PWA writes and native local-sync writes converge on the same authorized Convex data without duplicate, missing, cross-user, or accounting-divergent records.
All money remains integer cents; all five split types retain existing rounding behavior; transfer/adjustment/system types and source provenance remain compatible.

Every `rules.md` contract is protected by automated tests and browser/real-device scenarios: share ledger only, payer cashflow, non-payer behavior, settlement movement, idempotent derivation, preserved account choice, transaction visibility, derived-row editing restrictions, current-user identity, and local/shared parity.
PWA is tested on an actual iPhone in Safari and installed mode; successful desktop rendering is only graceful support, not a claim of a completed desktop product.
Existing native Expo paths remain buildable and preserve their local-first guest/sync behavior; no native release is produced in this effort.
No production Convex deployment, EAS build/submit, DNS/hosting change, external account configuration, commit, or push occurs without explicit maintainer approval after the evidence is reviewable.
The dirty import work remains recoverable and untouched unless the user explicitly chooses a reviewed subset to include.
agent_notes: Planning-only authorization now covers Planthing publication and a surgical repository `plan.md` PWA checklist after publication. It does not authorize implementation or release writes.
The PWA branch/base name is an intended convention, not a command to create it until the implementation is authorized and git baseline verification is possible.
Use the documented dev Convex deployment for development-only function/schema pushes. Never run generic `npx convex deploy` when development is intended.
Production Convex backup/deploy and all hosting/domain configuration are maintainer-controlled release gates. EAS build/submit remains maintainer-only under repository rules.
Do not put real URLs, tokens, Clerk keys, Convex deploy keys, API keys, exports, database files, or user financial data into the plan, screenshots, patch snapshots, or test fixtures.

If user scope changes to offline web support, self-hosted services, a different identity provider, or desktop-first design, stop and create a revision: each changes core architecture and acceptance criteria.

When applying the `plan.md` checklist, prepend only the new PWA section, retain every older plan below it, leave every implementation checkbox unchecked, and byte-compare the pre-existing suffix because git diff is unavailable until the Xcode license is accepted by the maintainer.
